subject.title: [Bug] Sandbox validateEnvVarValue base64 heuristic false-positives on legitimate long alphanumeric values

question: Should OpenClaw narrow the sandbox env credential-data warning to structured base64 values on credential-looking env names, accepting fewer warnings for neutral or nonstandard names?
rationale: The false positive is source-reproducible, but the fix changes advisory sandbox credential-warning coverage, so automation cannot choose the security tradeoff.

options.title: Approve narrowed warning policy
options.body: Refresh the linked PR onto current main and land the key-aware structured-base64 sanitizer if sandbox/security owners accept reduced neutral-name warnings.

options.title: Preserve broader warning coverage
options.body: Keep this issue open and request a different heuristic that reduces false positives without requiring credential-like names.

options.title: Declare the warning intentional
options.body: Close the issue as not planned only if maintainers decide broad value-only warnings are the desired sandbox safety policy.

recommendation.title: Approve narrowed warning policy
recommendation.body: Refresh the linked PR onto current main and land the key-aware structured-base64 sanitizer if sandbox/security owners accept reduced neutral-name warnings.

likelyOwner.reason: The sanitizer introduction and warning-threshold history make this the strongest available routing candidate for the security-boundary choice.
